bugs.error_message: runtime.test.ts > position > clamps negative and non-finite input to the start: AssertionError: expected false to be true (position(TABATA, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY).isComplete)
bugs.root_cause: Test expectation was wrong, not the implementation. position() guards with `Number.isFinite(elapsedMs) ? Math.max(0, elapsedMs) : 0`, so +Infinity is rejected as invalid input and clamps to 0 rather than being read as 'past the end' and completing the workout.
bugs.fix: Kept the implementation and corrected the test: ALL non-finite input (NaN, -Infinity, +Infinity) clamps to the start. One rule for invalid input beats two special cases, and a real monotonic clock never produces these values. Documented the rule in the test and in position()'s doc comment.

bugs.error_message: Idle run screen rendered the 'Ready' panel AND a live countdown simultaneously, putting 4 children into a 3-row grid
bugs.root_cause: position(timeline, 0) legitimately returns the FIRST entry, not null — only completion yields a null entry. So `at.entry` is truthy before the workout starts, and gating the running body on `entry &&` alone was true during 'idle'.
bugs.fix: Derive `const isRunning = status === 'running' || status === 'paused'` and gate on `isRunning ? at.entry : null`. Same flag unlights the effort strip when idle (currentIndex -1).

bugs.error_message: Skipping a step while paused (or stepping back from complete) left the clock advancing, so the next Resume credited a huge bogus pause and jumped the workout forward
bugs.root_cause: seekTo() re-anchored startedAt but only refreshed pausedAt if it was already non-zero. Stepping back from 'complete' set status to 'paused' while pausedAt stayed 0, so readElapsed() kept using now() — the clock ran while the UI said paused, and resume() then added (now - 0).
bugs.fix: seekTo takes an explicit `freeze` flag (`status !== 'running'`) and always sets pausedAt accordingly. Also extracted the whole arithmetic into pure src/state/clock.ts (Clock + elapsed/started/paused/resumed/seeked) with 11 unit tests that need no DOM — including one named for this bug.

bugs.error_message: max-height: 40cqh on the media panel had no container to resolve against
bugs.root_cause: `.run` declares `container-type: inline-size`, which establishes an INLINE-axis query container only. cqh needs `container-type: size` (which requires a definite block size). With no eligible container, cqh silently falls back to the small viewport — right by accident, wrong by intent.
bugs.fix: Use `min(40svh, 26rem)` explicitly. Rule: with container-type: inline-size, only cqi/cqw are meaningful.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED: 'the countdown and image panels need to be responsive and size to occupy the available screen space. they're tiny on my laptop'
bugs.root_cause: Both were capped in rem, so a big screen was wasted. `.count__clock` was clamp(5rem, 34cqi, 15rem) — on a 1440px laptop 34cqi computes to ~490px and the 15rem ceiling chopped it to 240px. The media column was minmax(16rem, 22rem), hard-capped at 352px. Neither considered available HEIGHT at all, and `.run` was container-type: inline-size so cqh was not even available.
bugs.fix: Named containers (`shell` / inline-size for layout switching, `body` / size on .run__body so BOTH axes are queryable — safe because a 1fr row of a 100%-height grid has a definite block size). Countdown is now max(3rem, min(calc(84cqi / var(--chars)), 52cqh)) with --chars set from the string's em width (digit 1, colon 0.5) so '8' and '17' match while '4:30' steps down. Columns became minmax(0, 3fr) minmax(0, 2fr); the panel frame drops aspect-ratio on wide layouts and stretches to the row height with object-fit: contain.
bugs.fix_rule: Do not cap a hero element in rem. Size it against both axes with cq units and let content length, not an arbitrary ceiling, be the limit.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED: 'make all the small text much bigger' — labels, meta rows, button text and stats were unreadable
bugs.root_cause: The --label token was `600 0.7rem/1.2` (~11.2px) with 0.16em tracking — a sensible size for a desktop dashboard, and a deliberate typographic counterweight to the giant numerals, but it ignored this app's actual requirement: readable across a gym, mid-effort, at 2-3 metres. Fixed rem sizing also meant it never grew on a large screen.
bugs.fix: --label-size is now clamp(1rem, 1.6cqi, 1.6rem), so ~11px became 16px on a phone and 23px on a laptop; tracking eased to 0.11em since the same tracking reads much wider at a larger size. Also enlarged: exercise name floor 1.25rem -> 1.75rem, stat figures to clamp(1.75rem, 4cqi, 3rem), primary button its own clamp(1.05rem, 1.9cqi, 1.9rem), chevron glyphs their own larger scale, button targets 56px -> 64px (primary 76px).
bugs.fix_rule: Type scale must follow the VIEWING DISTANCE, not convention. For anything read at arm's length or further, treat ~1rem as the floor for secondary text and let it scale with the container.

bugs.error_message: Control row would overflow a phone width once button text was enlarged (5 buttons, primary min-width 12rem, no wrapping)
bugs.root_cause: `.controls` was a nowrap flex row with `justify-content: center`, and `.btn--primary` had a fixed `min-width: 12rem`. At the enlarged label size the five buttons total ~550px against a 390px phone. Latent before the type change; the bigger text made it certain.
bugs.fix: Added `flex-wrap: wrap` so transport controls take the first line and Reset/Sound fall to the second, and changed the primary button to `min-width: min(12rem, 100%)` so a narrow screen cannot be forced wider than it is.
bugs.fix_rule: A fixed min-width inside a nowrap flex row is an overflow waiting to happen. Guard with min(target, 100%) and let the row wrap.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED: 'the progress bar on top - the muted red bars look brown'
bugs.root_cause: The effort strip used a single background colour with opacity per state (0.22 todo / 0.5 done / 1 current) over a near-black ground. Compositing a saturated hue down toward black is exactly how you make brown: red #EF4A3F at 22% resolves to #431F1D and at 50% to #802E2A. Green and blue muddied the same way, but red is the one that reads unmistakably as brown because dark desaturated red IS brown.
bugs.fix: Dropped opacity for explicit per-state backgrounds. Upcoming steps are neutral `var(--ink-600)` — their HEIGHT already encodes work vs rest, so hue was redundant. Completed steps keep hue but mix toward a LIGHT grey rather than down toward black: `color-mix(in oklab, var(--step-colour) 55%, var(--bone-dim))`, giving #C9716D for red. Only the current step is at full strength.
bugs.fix_rule: Never dim a saturated colour toward a near-black ground to indicate an inactive state. Mix toward a mid or light neutral to keep the hue readable, or drop the hue entirely.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED (with screenshot): 'the countdown numbers are not centered'
bugs.root_cause: CSS applies letter-spacing after EVERY character including the last, so with `letter-spacing: -0.045em` the line box is narrower than the visible glyphs by that amount. Centring the line box therefore leaves the glyphs offset by half of it — about 20px at a 459px font size, and visibly off next to the centred exercise name and meta row.
bugs.fix: Hoisted the value into `--tracking` and added `padding-right: calc(-1 * var(--tracking))` on the block. Narrowing the content box by the same amount shifts the centred line back by exactly half of it. Kept as one variable so the two can never drift apart.
bugs.fix_rule: Centred text with non-zero letter-spacing is always offset by half the tracking. Compensate on the block with padding equal to the letter-spacing, from a shared custom property.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED: 'when the number of digits reduces, the numbers get bigger pushing the rest of the content off the screen'
bugs.root_cause: clockWidth() returned the literal em width of the string, so a single digit gave 1 and the font size became `coef * 1cqi / 1` instead of `/ 2`. The width term then stopped binding, the height term took over, and '9' rendered up to 100% larger than '10' — measured +100% at 342x710, +73% at 342x560, +59% at 600x900. The coefficient had been calibrated for two digits all along. A test even asserted clockWidth('8') === 1 under the name 'sizes one and two digits so the countdown does not jump', so the test guaranteed the very jump its name denied.
bugs.fix: clockWidth now returns Math.max(2, units), so the size only ever steps DOWN for longer strings. Test corrected to assert the floor, plus a new test asserting the sequence is monotonically non-increasing.
bugs.fix_rule: When a size divides by a content-derived factor, floor that factor at the value the coefficient was calibrated for. Otherwise short content grows instead of long content shrinking.

bugs.error_message: Media panel pushed below the fold on a short narrow window (visible in the same screenshot — no image panel at all)
bugs.root_cause: In the stacked layout the panel frame had `aspect-ratio: 4/3` with `max-height: min(40svh, 26rem)`, so it demanded a height proportional to its WIDTH regardless of how much vertical space was left. Countdown + name + meta + a 4:3 panel simply exceeds a short body, and the overflow went off-screen silently.
bugs.fix: Dropped aspect-ratio and max-height entirely; the frame is `height: 100%` in both layouts. `.run__body` stacked is now `grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr)` so the countdown block takes what it needs and the panel absorbs the remainder. Also gave the clock its own `--clock-height` per layout: 40cqh stacked (the panel needs room below), 74cqh beside the panel. object-fit: contain means a smaller frame never distorts the image.
bugs.fix_rule: In a stacked layout, size the flexible element off REMAINING space (minmax(0,1fr) + height:100%), not off its own width via aspect-ratio.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED: 'the text on the cards is the wrong way around - the routine name should be bigger and the text below it smaller'
bugs.root_cause: `.label` was declared as `font: var(--label)` — the FONT SHORTHAND, which resets font-size. It lived in run-screen.css while `.row__meta` (which carries both classes) set its own smaller font-size in library.css. Equal specificity, so source order decided, and App.tsx imports LibraryScreen before RunScreen — so run-screen.css loaded last and `.label` silently clobbered the card's size. Card meta rendered at 44.5px against a 30.4px routine name on a laptop, inverted at every width.
bugs.fix: Moved `.label` and `.unit` to theme.css (loaded first by main.tsx, so components can override) and rewrote them with LONGHAND properties, so setting font-size or the --label-size token actually wins. `.row__meta` now steps down via `--label-size: var(--label-size-sm)`. Name/meta ratio is 1.5-2.07x depending on width.
bugs.fix_rule: Never use the `font:` shorthand in a shared utility class — it resets font-size and family, so any component override becomes import-order dependent. Shared utilities belong in the globally-first stylesheet, in longhand, parameterised by a custom property.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED: 'something is off with the combination of fonts - the home screen seems different to the routine screens'
bugs.root_cause: No shared type scale. An audit found 11 ad-hoc font-size expressions and 5 different letter-spacing values (-0.03, -0.02, -0.01, 0.06, 0.1, 0.11em) split across library.css and run-screen.css, each invented per element. The same role was styled differently per screen — uppercase labels tracked 0.06em on one and 0.11em on the other, and screen titles used unrelated sizes — so the two screens read as different apps.
bugs.fix: One scale in theme.css: three tracking tokens keyed to ROLE (--track-display -0.03em, --track-name -0.01em, --label-tracking 0.11em) and four size tokens (--size-display, --size-title, --size-name, --label-size plus --label-size-sm). Both stylesheets now reference tokens only; the sole remaining literal is .count__name, which needs a cqh term the tokens do not carry, and is commented as such.
bugs.fix_rule: Type scale belongs in the shared theme, keyed to role, before a second screen exists. Per-element clamps invented locally will diverge.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED: the next-up line sits flush against the controls divider; a 3px nudge appeared to do nothing
bugs.root_cause: `.run__body` in the STACKED layout had `padding: var(--step-5) var(--step-5) 0` — zero bottom padding — so the panel's bottom edge met the controls' border-top directly. The 3px margin DID apply (measurable as ~6 device px at 2x in the screenshot), it was simply the entire clearance that existed. The wide layout was fine because it has 24px bottom padding.
bugs.fix: Gave the stacked body `var(--step-4)` (16px) bottom padding and removed the 3px margin as redundant. Fixing the missing padding rather than stacking a nudge on top of a zero.
bugs.fix_rule: When a nudge appears to do nothing, check what it is being added to. A margin against zero padding is the whole gap, not an adjustment to one.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED: 'the sound after the 3s countdown is supposed to sound like a bell but it sounds like a click'
bugs.root_cause: TWO causes. (1) The envelope was a single exponential from peak, which is loud in the middle and silent by 500ms. Re-measuring the app's bell showed the real shape is a STRIKE plus a RING: it drops to 0.33 of peak within 25ms and is still audible at 1200ms. A single exponential is a tone being switched off; the quiet long tail is what makes it a bell. (2) `cancelPending()` stopped EVERY tracked oscillator including ones already sounding, and the scheduler re-arms its window every 10 seconds — so any cue overlapping a re-arm was cut off mid-ring, which is itself an audible click. With phase changes every 10-20s in a Tabata, collisions were frequent.
bugs.fix: Note gained `sustain` (fraction of peak the strike falls to) and `strikeMs`, so the envelope is attack -> strike -> long tail. Bell is now sustain 0.33, strikeMs 22, durationMs 2050, with the inharmonic partial given decayScale 0.45 because high partials die before the body stops ringing. And `pending` became a Map of node -> scheduled start time, so `cancelPending` skips anything already sounding and only drops future cues.
bugs.fix_rule: A percussive sound needs a two-part envelope: brief loud transient, then a much quieter long tail. And never stop a sounding oscillator to re-arm a scheduler — cutting audio mid-ring is a click.

bugs.error_message: First FFT pass reported six 'partials' for each cue that were really adjacent bins of two peaks
bugs.root_cause: Took the top-6 spectral bins by magnitude with no minimum separation, so spectral leakage around a single peak filled the list (511/517/519/527/529/531 Hz is one tone, not six). It happened to identify the right two partials for the bell, but it could easily have missed a weaker lower fundamental.
bugs.fix: Re-ran peak-picking with a 40Hz minimum separation and reported relative magnitudes, which confirmed the bell is genuinely just 2659Hz at 1.00 and 6854Hz at 0.39.
bugs.fix_rule: When picking spectral peaks, enforce a minimum separation. Adjacent bins are one peak.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED: 'the countdown is still changing size when it transitions from 1:00 to 59 and squashing the image'
bugs.root_cause: TWO causes, both left over from bug-010's partial fix. (1) `--chars` was computed from the CURRENT clock string, so a step counting through the minute boundary went from '1:00' (3.5 units) to '59' (2 units) and the font grew ~75% mid-step. Flooring at 2 had only fixed the single-digit case. (2) The stacked layout used `grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr)`, so the countdown block took whatever height it needed and the image absorbed the rest — meaning any change in numeral size resized the picture.
bugs.fix: `--chars` now comes from the step's LONGEST string — clockWidth(clock(ceil(entry.durationMs / 1000))) — so it is constant for the whole step and the countdown cannot change size while running. And the stacked split is fixed proportions (56fr / 44fr) instead of auto, so the image never moves. Because the countdown now only gets 56% of the body while cqh still measures the whole body, --clock-height came down from 40cqh to 34cqh; verified the count block fits its row at six window sizes including 342x380.
bugs.fix_rule: Size a countdown from the LONGEST value it will display, never the current one — otherwise it resizes as digits drop. And in a stacked layout, give a flexible neighbour a fixed proportion rather than the remainder, or it moves whenever its sibling does.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED: 'on a small screen can you shrink the image to fit the available space?'
bugs.root_cause: Not an overflow — the image was already contained. The exercise illustrations are near-square (876x800 measured from the real file), so a SHORT WIDE frame fits them to its height and leaves the width unused: at a 342x103 frame the picture rendered at 0.13x, tiny inside a large empty bordered box. The fixed 56/44 stacked split gave the panel the same share regardless of how little vertical space there was.
bugs.fix: Two viewport-height tiers hand space to the image on short screens: at <=700px the split becomes 50/50 with --clock-height 28cqh, and at <=540px it becomes 46/54 with 22cqh plus lower name and label FLOORS (those floors, not the countdown, are what crowd the row at that height). Image renders 19-47% larger depending on size; a normal phone portrait (390x844) is unchanged. Declared before the wide container block, since the two-column layout overrides both rows and --clock-height and must not be affected.
bugs.fix_rule: `object-fit: contain` fits the SMALLER axis, so a box whose aspect ratio is far from the image's wastes the other axis. When the content is near-square, the box's aspect ratio matters more than its area.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED (screenshot): the exercise image is vertically truncated — the bottom of the picture is cut off at the frame edge
bugs.root_cause: `.panel__frame img` had `width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: contain`, but as a normal grid item its `height: 100%` was resolving to AUTO. The box therefore took the image's natural aspect at full width (463x423 for an 876x800 image in a 463px frame), grew taller than the frame's 295px, and `overflow: hidden` cut the bottom off. `object-fit: contain` never letterboxed anything, because the box it was fitting into was already too tall. I had twice reasoned that 'contain means it cannot overflow' — which is only true once the box itself is bounded.
bugs.fix: The image is absolutely positioned with `inset: 0` inside a `position: relative` frame. An absolutely-positioned box takes its dimensions from the containing block directly, so the height is definite regardless of the grid, and contain then shrinks the picture to fit — full height, letterboxed at the sides.
bugs.fix_rule: `object-fit` only constrains the picture WITHIN the element's box; it does nothing about the box itself. If a replaced element's percentage height may resolve to auto, use `position: absolute; inset: 0` to make the box definite, or the natural aspect will overflow and be clipped.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED: 'the save button is invisible' (editor header)
bugs.root_cause: `.btn--primary` is `color: var(--ink-900); background: var(--phase)`, and `--phase` was only ever set as an inline style on `.run`. In the editor it is undefined, and an undefined custom property makes the whole `background` declaration INVALID at computed-value time — so the background fell back to transparent and the button rendered as dark text on a dark ground.
bugs.fix: Gave `--phase` a root default of `var(--role-rest)` in theme.css; the run screen still overrides it per step. Also moved `.btn*` and `.chip*` out of run-screen.css / library.css into theme.css, since three screens use them and they only worked from a screen-specific file because the bundler concatenates all CSS.
bugs.fix_rule: A custom property consumed outside the subtree that sets it needs a root default (or a `var(x, fallback)`), or the whole declaration silently drops. And a class used by more than one screen belongs in the shared stylesheet, not in whichever screen defined it first.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED: 'the fourth sound after a round is also broken like the other one was' — the workout-complete figure was truncated
bugs.root_cause: The completion cue is SEVEN notes spread over ~3.45s, queued as separate oscillators at future times. It fires at exactly totalMs — the same instant the timer sets status to 'complete', which re-runs the scheduler effect and called cancelPending(). The earlier fix spared oscillators whose OWN start time had passed, so the first note survived and every later note of the same figure was stopped. Per-note reasoning fixed the single-note bell and left the multi-note fanfare broken in exactly the same way.
bugs.fix: Cancellation is judged per CUE, not per note: every oscillator is tagged with the moment its cue began, and a cue that has begun is left entirely alone including its remaining notes. Added a 0.15s grace so tick-versus-audio-clock skew cannot cancel a figure a hair before it starts, and added deduplication in the scheduler (keyed `kind@atMs`) so a spared cue cannot be re-queued by the next arm and played twice.
bugs.fix_rule: When a cue is a FIGURE rather than a single sound, cancellation has to reason about the figure. Track the group, not the note.

bugs.error_message: USER REPORTED: the image placeholder text is truncated on a portrait iPad
bugs.root_cause: `fitCqi`'s coefficient was 161, derived as 100 / 0.62 — two optimistic assumptions compounded. Bold uppercase advances nearer 0.68-0.72em, not 0.62, and the calculation used the FULL container width while `.panel__empty` had 12px of fixed padding either side. On a portrait iPad the wide layout gives the panel only ~250px, where 24px of padding is a tenth of the width, so every fallback name overflowed by about 20% and was clipped by the frame's overflow: hidden. It fitted on a laptop purely because the panel is twice as wide there and the padding proportionally trivial.
bugs.fix: Padding is proportional on both axes (`4cqh 4cqi`), so the available share is a constant 92% at any size. The coefficient is now an explicit budget over an explicit advance — 84 of the 92 available, divided by a 0.72em advance — and the gap between 84 and 92 is where all the safety lives, because the sizing maths is exact by construction. Added `overflow-wrap: anywhere` so a wider-than-assumed font breaks a word rather than clipping it, and a test asserting the fit holds against a PESSIMISTIC 0.78em advance, since testing against the assumed advance would prove nothing.
bugs.fix_rule: When sizing text by arithmetic, the assumed glyph advance is the whole risk. Leave an explicit margin between what the text claims and what is available, and test against a wider advance than you assumed.

bugs.error_message: Tinted library rows lost their hover feedback entirely
bugs.root_cause: `.row[data-clickable='true']:hover` sets a flat `background`, and the new `.row[data-colour]:not([data-confirming='true'])` tint rule TIES with it on specificity. Source order alone decided it, and the tint came later, so hover never applied to a coloured row.
bugs.fix: Added an explicit tinted-hover rule mixing the same wash into the lighter --ink-700 ground. Delete-confirm is excluded from the tint via :not() rather than by source order.
bugs.fix_rule: When two rules tie on specificity, order decides. Encode precedence with :not() instead of relying on where a block sits in the file.

bugs.error_message: A truncated download was read as a genuinely smaller image (179KB vs 477KB)
bugs.root_cause: A curl hit the 2-minute command timeout and left a partial PNG. Its size and sha256 were then compared as evidence, making two identical images look very different. PIL exposed it: 'image file is truncated'.
bugs.fix: Re-downloaded with an explicit --max-time inside the command budget and decoded before comparing.
bugs.fix_rule: Confirm a downloaded file DECODES before treating its size or hash as evidence of anything.

bugs.error_message: imageCatalogue.ts claimed duplicate-named images were 'genuinely different images'
bugs.root_cause: The claim was written when the file was created and never checked. Both pairs are re-uploads of one photograph: aligned for a 1px crop they differ 1.8/255 and 3.3/255 mean, where genuinely different plates differ 16.6/255.
bugs.fix: Removed both duplicates (27 images), corrected the comment to state what was measured, repointed 6 references in two seeded routines at the canonical URL, added two guard tests.
bugs.fix_rule: Never write a comment asserting a fact that was not measured. A confident comment outlives the assumption behind it.

bugs.error_message: Rattle rate reported as SLOWING to 9.6Hz when the time axis was compressed
bugs.root_cause: Compressing time can only raise a modulation rate. The FFT window was the ~127ms compressed steady portion, too short to resolve 18Hz from 24Hz, so it locked onto an envelope component. A peak-counting cross-check was wrong twice too (115Hz, then 48Hz, against a true 18Hz) because one rattle cycle has several local maxima.
bugs.fix: Measure the final tiled 700ms curve, and return NaN when the window is under 250ms rather than guessing. Peak-count measure deleted with a comment recording why. FFT validated by tracking RATTLE proportionally across x1.18/x1.32/x1.48.
bugs.fix_rule: Check a measurement against the direction the physics demands. If a result is impossible, the instrument is wrong, not the signal.

bugs.error_message: Committed generator could not run from the repo: FileNotFoundError 'amp.npy'
bugs.root_cause: Hardcoded bare input filenames and an absolute output path, so it only ran from the scratchpad it was written in.
bugs.fix: Paths resolved relative to __file__, ANALYSIS_DIR override, and a real error message instead of a numpy traceback. scripts/.analysis/ gitignored because full-rate amplitude+frequency of the Tabata mp3 is effectively a copy of it.
bugs.fix_rule: A script committed to the repo must run from the repo. Resolve paths relative to __file__, never to the cwd it was authored in.

bugs.error_message: Large gap between the 'Routine text' label and its textarea in the paste dialog
bugs.root_cause: Both children of .paste__field were auto grid rows, and a grid stretches auto tracks to absorb spare height, so the label's row grew with the dialog and left the label at the top of it.
bugs.fix: grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr) on .paste__field - label sized to its text, control taking the rest.
bugs.fix_rule: An auto grid track absorbs spare height. Declare the tracks when one child should grow and the other should not.

bugs.error_message: Paste dialog looked bottom-heavy: too much space above the buttons
bugs.root_cause: grid-template-rows declared five tracks but the dialog has four children when the parse report is absent, and an empty explicit track still takes its gap.
bugs.fix: Three explicit tracks with the rest implicit, so there are exactly as many tracks as children.
bugs.fix_rule: Declare only the tracks you always have. An empty explicit track is invisible but still costs a gap.

bugs.error_message: Confirm dialog rendered nearly full-height, with its two buttons stretched into 280px slabs
bugs.root_cause: A dialog is a DOM child of the full-height grid screen that opened it. Stretched by that grid, .notice's three auto rows split the spare height between them - title pinned to the top, detail marooned in the middle, buttons at the bottom - and .notice__actions, being a stretched flex container, pulled its chips to full height as well.
bugs.fix: height: fit-content plus align-self: center and align-content: center on .notice so the rows pack; align-items: center on .notice__actions so the chips keep their own height.
bugs.fix_rule: Never trust a box to be sized by its contents when an ancestor is a grid or flex container. Auto grid rows and flex children both stretch by default. Same class as bug-028 and bug-029.

bugs.error_message: On a short narrow window the step name pushed 'Step 8 / 179' out of the count column and behind the media panel
bugs.root_cause: The countdown and the step name share one column but were sized independently: the clock claimed 34cqh and a two-line name another 22cqh, more than the 56fr row holds. .count's lead track was a bare 1fr, whose min-content floor meant the grid grew past its parent row rather than giving way, so the meta row landed under the panel below.
bugs.fix: A --name-lines custom property, set from nameLines(entry.name), subtracts 11cqh from the clock's cap for every line past the first - in the stacked layout and the two-column one. .count's lead track is minmax(0, 1fr) so it can shrink.
bugs.fix_rule: Two elements sharing a column must be sized against each other, not each against the column. A bare 1fr has a min-content floor; use minmax(0, 1fr) wherever the content may be taller than the track.

bugs.error_message: Exporting a pasted routine and re-importing it silently dropped it: 'no readable routines'
bugs.root_cause: isBlock is a WHITELIST - it accepted only 'segment' and 'repeat'. When ladders and sections were added it was not updated, so isWorkout rejected every pasted routine and fromBundle's .filter(isWorkout) discarded it. The export itself wrote the routine out perfectly, so the backup looked valid and restored nothing.
bugs.fix: isBlock accepts every kind in GROUP_KINDS (repeat, ladder, section) and validates their children. Round-trip test added over a real pasted routine.
bugs.fix_rule: Adding a block kind means updating every whitelist that validates one - bundle.ts is the only strict validator; shareLink.ts checks only that blocks is an array.

bugs.error_message: The first whistle of a workout — the one at the end of the get-ready — played the plain 2900Hz fallback tone instead of the recording
bugs.root_cause: A cue is BUILT when it is scheduled, not when it sounds: playNote reads this.samples.get(name) at schedule time and creates either a buffer source or the synthesised fallback there and then. unlock() starts the whistle fetch+decode without awaiting it, and useCueScheduler's first arm() runs synchronously in the same tick, queueing the whole 30s lookahead window before the bytes could possibly land. Dedup via `scheduled` then means those cues are never revisited, so every whistle in the first half-minute kept the fallback. It only looked intermittent because any clock mutation (pause, resume, skip, seek) bumps `generation`, which clears the dedup set and requeues with the recording.
bugs.fix: Two parts. (1) samples.ts starts the download at module load and exposes sampleBytes() — the network is the slow half and needs no AudioContext, so it does not wait for the gesture. (2) engine.onSampleDecoded() notifies when a buffer lands; the scheduler cancels pending, forgets the keys requeueable() says were actually dropped, and re-arms. requeueable() shares CANCEL_GRACE_MS with cancelPending so a cue already sounding is spared rather than queued twice.
bugs.fix_rule: Anything read at SCHEDULE time is frozen for up to LOOKAHEAD_MS. If a scheduling input can change after the fact (a decode, a setting, a tint), it must announce itself and the window must be re-armed — and any re-arm that clears the dedup set has to respect the same grace cancelPending() uses, or a sounding cue plays twice.

bugs.error_message: Choosing images for two steps in a row shared ONE undo step — one press of undo took both pictures back
bugs.root_cause: patchSegment passed `coalesce = patch.role === undefined`, i.e. 'anything that is not the role is text'. A media patch from the picker, the upload or the link field therefore coalesced, and history.push replaces the present when the previous push was also coalescible. So a second image pick overwrote the first entry, and any image pick following a typing run was absorbed into it. The coalescing flag was also a single global boolean, so typing in two different fields collapsed together.
bugs.fix: history.push now takes the FIELD being typed into (string | null) instead of a boolean, and only replaces the present when the field matches. isTypedPatch (editor/blocks.ts) names the only keystroke-by-keystroke field on a step — name — so media, role, note and alternative are discrete. The timing NUMBER box now coalesces (it is typed) while the unit select stays discrete.
bugs.fix_rule: Coalescing must be keyed on the field, never on a 'this was text' flag: a shared flag silently merges unrelated edits and swallows any non-typing action that rides the same path. When adding a patch route, ask whether the field fires per keystroke — if not, it is discrete.

bugs.error_message: Focusing the image link field of a step with an uploaded photo and tabbing away deleted the photo; blurring an unchanged note left an undo step that undid nothing
bugs.root_cause: Both fields commit on blur and committed unconditionally. commitUrl treated an empty box as 'clear the image' — but the box is ALWAYS empty for a local (uploaded) image, since mediaUrl() only returns a URL for source 'remote'. commitText re-patched the same note, and clearText on an absent field still returns a new tree, so either way push() stored a state identical to the present.
bugs.fix: commitText returns when the trimmed value matches what is stored. commitUrl clears only when the media is source 'remote', returns on an unrecognised link, and writes only when the normalised URL differs from the current one. The new × in the field is the deliberate way to remove any image, including an uploaded one.
bugs.fix_rule: A blur-committed field must compare against stored state before writing, or focus alone becomes an edit. And never infer 'the user cleared it' from an empty control that was never populated for that data shape.

bugs.error_message: User-reported: after starting a routine by CLICKING play, the right arrow key did not skip — starting it with the spacebar and the arrows worked
bugs.root_cause: The keyboard handler bailed out on `tag === 'INPUT' || tag === 'BUTTON' || tag === 'SELECT'`. Clicking a control leaves it focused, so every later keydown targets a <button> and EVERY shortcut was dropped, arrows included. Starting with the spacebar left focus on <body>, so the same session had a working keyboard. The guard's stated intent was only to stop space double-firing on a focused button.
bugs.fix: Extracted `shortcutApplies(tagName, key)` to src/ui/keys.ts: a field or select takes every key, a button takes only Space and Enter (which activate it), and the arrows / m / k always belong to the screen. Tested without a DOM.
bugs.fix_rule: A focus guard has to name the KEYS the focused thing consumes, not just its tag. 'Ignore all keys while X has focus' silently disables every unrelated shortcut, and the failure mode is silence — nothing logs, nothing throws.
